correctness.rationale: Writing p(t)=Pr(X1>t) and q(a,b)=Pr(X1>a,X2>b), covariance equals n[p(b)(1-n p(a))+(n-1)q(a,b)]. Conditional X1/(1-X2)|X2 is Beta(alpha,(n-2)alpha), whose upper-tail probability decreases strictly as X2 increases; q(a,b)/p(b) decreases strictly to 0 as b approaches 1-a. The initial covariance at b=a is Var(K_a)>0; final sign comes from 1-np(a). The asymptotic expansion of one- and two-coordinate normalized-Gamma densities gives h2(t,u)-h1(t)-h1(u)=-(t-alpha)(u-alpha), a checked symbolic identity, hence the limiting p_y(1-p_x)-c_x c_y/alpha. Its unique limiting crossing follows from the strictly increasing Gamma tail-density ratio. The independently rebuilt alpha=1 exact-power covariance and root formula were checked across dimensions 3..10; this is only corroboration for all real alpha.

final_claim: For symmetric Dirichlet(alpha,...,alpha), n>=3 and all alpha>0, the covariance of nested threshold counts has exactly one positive-to-negative crossing in the upper threshold precisely for lower thresholds below the quantile p(a)=1/n. There are an explicit alpha=1 formula and a fixed-alpha asymptotic Gamma covariance with one crossing.
